item.title: @sothebys: 97 years ago today, this Norman Rockwell illustration graced the cover of The Saturday Eve
item.author: @sothebys
item.description:
97 years ago today, this Norman Rockwell illustration graced the cover of The Saturday Evening Post. It’s a clever commentary on the 1920s Jazz Age, and after over 30 years in private hands, it makes its auction debut at #SothebysNewYork.
Rockwell created 321 cover illustrations for The Post over a 47-year period. This work is the final time that James K. Van Brunt, one of Rockwell’s favorite subjects, modeled for the artist. Here, Rockwell depicts him as a violinist enticed to buy a saxophone, a defining symbol of the Jazz Age. In drawing a classical musician tempted by the new instrument of the day, Rockwell sets up the narrative tension and humor which defined his great Post covers.
‘Man Looking at Saxophone (Jazz It Up with a Sax)’ is a highlight of The Modern Day Auction, presented in partnership with @celine. Register to bid in the 19 November sale at the link in bio.

How does an exhibition become a book? What does it mean to translate an artist’s vision, a body of work, or an archive into a printed object?
Join multi-hyphenate designers Sablā Stays (@callmesabla) and Arsh Raziuddin (@arshraziuddin) for a conversation about the art of making books. Taking two recent New Museum exhibition catalogs, Arthur Jafa’s “I Am Tony” and “The Bowery: Devil’s Mile”, as their starting point, the designers will explore how typography, materiality, visual references, and editorial decisions shape the tactile ways we encounter art and history.
This program is free with admission. Copies of both publications will be available for purchase and signing following the conversation.
Get tickets via the link in bio 🔗

Her collaborators and clients have included The New York Times, The Atlantic, Condé Nast, Nike, Bloomberg, A24, New York City Hall, Penguin Random House, Hachette, and Simon & Schuster.
Most recently, Raziuddin led the creative direction and design of New York City’s official FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign in partnership with New York City Hall. Her work has been recognized by the National Magazine Awards, the Society of Publication Designers, the Art Directors Club, Monocle, Print, and The New York Times. She previously taught publication design in MICA’s MFA program and continues to explore how design can shape culture, participation, and collective memory.

item.title: @pennmuseum: How should international organizations confront cultural heritage preservation as part of
item.author: @pennmuseum
item.description:
How should international organizations confront cultural heritage preservation as part of their missions during modern military conflict?
Dr. Lynn Meskell gets right to the heart of that question with her forthcoming book, “Ruined: The Heritage of War from UNESCO to NATO,” (Oxford University Press, November 2027) as she shines a light on the seizure and destruction of cultural heritage in places such as Gaza and Ukraine—where the past has become weaponized and targeted.
Dr. Meskell is a curator in the Penn Museum’s Middle East and Asia sections, Penn Integrates Knowledge professor, Richard D. Green Professor in Anthropology in the School of Arts and Sciences, Professor in Historic Preservation at the Weitzman School of Design, and a leading researcher in the politics and ethics of cultural heritage.
“Ruined” traces the history of protecting heritage is a requirement for agencies guarding against illicit trafficking, terror financing, cultural cleansing, and crimes against humanity—yet, at the same time, it can be weaponized to push for more conflict. It demonstrates how heritage assets once thought of as “global goods” have now turned into tools of war.

item.title: @sothebys: This is how to look at Ed Ruscha’s 1964 painting ‘Dimple.’ With just six letters, Ruscha e
item.author: @sothebys
item.description:
This is how to look at Ed Ruscha’s 1964 painting ‘Dimple.’ With just six letters, Ruscha explores exactly what a word can do in a painting.
Here, Sotheby’s David Galperin analyzes the power of Ruscha’s clamp. ‘Dimple’ is one of only seven paintings featuring his rare and important C-clamp motif, which squeezes the final 'e' here. It radically disrupts the flatness of the text, giving it both a sculptural physicality and surreal bent. With this act of subversion, Ruscha elevates text into object, language into art, colloquialism into critique.
‘Dimple’ is a highlight of Vision: The Extraordinary Collection of Theodore and Ruth Baum coming to #SothebysNewYork on 16 November. Register to bid in the evening auction, presented in partnership with @celine, at the link in bio.

item.author: @newstudioarchitecture
item.description:
Our Artist Spotlight series continues with @ceyadams, a visual artist and graphic designer whose work spans more than 40 years.
Starting as a graffiti artist in the '80s, Cey became the creative director at @defjam, where he created logos, brand identities, tour backdrops, merchandise, and more. He later returned to the studio, combining his love of graphic design with his talents in graffiti and street art in his collage series, titled Trusted Brands. He’s collaborated with national brands and painted murals across the country, including in St. Paul’s @cezmsp.
Cey was introduced to our team while visiting St. Paul to exhibit Trusted Brands. That introduction grew into a lasting friendship, bringing him back to @newstudiogallery over the years to share his work, including his full-scale exhibition, Cey Adams: ETCetera, 40 Years of Art and Design. His work and friendship continue to be an important part of our space and St. Paul's creative community.

This year’s Benefit Auction comes at a critical time in SI’s history as we celebrate our 40th anniversary and prepare to move into a permanent new home on the Bowery in 2027.

Theaster Gates has forged a singular and profoundly expansive vision of art, uniting conceptual formalism, sculpture, performance, land art, and urbanism. At the heart of his practice is the preservation and critical reactivation of culturally significant Black spaces and objects, most notably through his landmark projects on Chicago’s South Side, where disused and dispossessed buildings have been transformed into publicly accessible archives, listening spaces, libraries, centers for experimental practice, and sites of collective gathering. For Gates, value emerges not from exclusivity, but through circulation, ritual, trade, care, and shared use, placing his work in close dialogue with the principles of a gift economy.

item.title: [Opening] @nostudiosmke: Artistic Director Norwood “PJ” Pennewell of Garth Fagan Dance talks about the power of sti
item.author: @nostudiosmke
item.description:
Artistic Director Norwood “PJ” Pennewell of Garth Fagan Dance talks about the power of stillness in dance. For Pennewell, stillness isn’t about counting seconds in your head, it’s about moving in rhythm with the music. He points to the company’s piece Never Top 40 and recalls how Garth Fagan explained the idea to his dancers, often saying: “I don’t want to see vacuous dancers.”
Garth Fagan Dance returns to The Joyce Theater November 4-8, 2026, for its 55th season, with its signature fusion of modern, post-modern, Afro-Caribbean, and ballet influences. The company honors Distinguished Artistic Director Emeritus Garth Fagan, recipient of the 2025 Bessie Award for Lifetime Achievement and the Tony Award-winning choreographer behind Disney’s The Lion King. Program highlights include Fagan’s seminal Prelude: Discipline is Freedom and the evocative Never Top 40, returning to New York City for the first time since 2001. Two NYC premieres expand the company’s vision: Priestess Hill by Pennewell and Messages To The Storm by Executive Director Natalie Rogers-Cropper.
Watch the full interview on YouTube: https://youtu.be/xK2g2PFcsyA

Almine Rech is pleased to announce that artist Joseph Kosuth has launched a new site-specific permanent installation ‘Maxima Proposito (Ovidio)’ at Palazzo Luce in Lecce, Italy! The new installation is made as a tribute to Lecce and Apulia.
@josephkosuthstudio @palazzoluce
•
Palazzo Luce presents a site-specific project by Joseph Kosuth, a leading figure of conceptual art. The work features red neon signs with selected passages from Ovid, shown in Latin and English, designed to engage in a dialogue between written text, light and the historic architecture of the palace courtyard.
The inauguration took place at dusk with a ceremonial lighting; the artist was present. The installation links the layered history of the city — evoking ancient Lupiae and nearby Augustan-era monuments — with contemporary artistic practices focused on language.

item.description:
Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026 at 7PM Film Screening and Election Night Afterparty
Co-presented with The NEW MUSEUM ELECTION NIGHT at MAYSLES + BLKNEWS: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Kahlil Joseph, 2025, 113 min., USA
As America watches the election returns, Maysles Documentary Center invites audiences to experience a different kind of news.
Kahlil Joseph’s BLKNWS: TERMS & CONDITIONS (2025) is a visionary exploration of Black history, memory, and imagination. Combining archival footage, music, contemporary media, and speculative storytelling, Joseph constructs a radical alternative to conventional news and historical narratives, one in which Black life becomes the center rather than the margins of the story.
Co-presented with The New Museum, who presented Khalil Joseph’s exhibition Shadow Play in 2017 and are currently presenting BLKNWS collaborator Arthur Jafa’s major survey exhibition, I Am Tony, the screening highlights artists challenging conventional ways of seeing and representing Black experience, drawing upon the emotional power of images, the rhythms of Black music, and the possibilities of cinema to imagine new forms of collective memory and consciousness.
On a night dominated by electoral maps, political punditry, and competing visions of America’s future, BLKNWS invites us to consider another question: Who gets to tell our stories, and what becomes possible when we control the images?
Join us following the screening for a post-election gathering and celebration at Maysles Documentary Center!

Instead of dreaming of Hollywood, Greta Lee fantasized about finding her own bohemia. She wanted to be an artist. “I wanted to be part of something cool," she says, "which to me was just about finding a thing that was greater than me and something that I could really get behind in an authentic way.”

Installation continues for ELLA WALKER’S “The Street,” the artist’s third solo exhibition at the gallery, opening this Thursday November 5th, from: 6-8pm, and on view through January 9th.
“The Street,” a new body of work roused from a lucid dream of remembered places and human intrigue set halfway between the Renaissance and present day.
Across five large scale paintings, a cast of characters move through brick-lined streets with uncanny spatial logic, fragmenting their bodies into a palimpsest of limbs, faces, and disembodied hands.
Layered and diluted paint flows in translucent swathes of color dammed by assertive outlines, occasionally revealing the ghostly pentimenti of an altered pose or worked-over figure.
Introducing contemporary costumes and observed environments, Walker’s expanded visual language grounds and reinvents the drama of an interior self set loose in the outside world.

item.author: @schomburgcenter
item.description:
Ragtime and jazz pianist and composer Eubie Blake (1887–1983) and jazz lyricist and composer Noble Sissle (1889–1975) were two of the artists featured in the film Once Upon a Time in Harlem. Filmed at Duke Ellington’s home in 1972, filmmaker William Greaves held a cocktail party that included most of the last living legends of the Harlem Renaissance and their supporters.
Blake and Sissle are perhaps most famous for their 1921 collaboration Shuffle Along. Blake wrote the lyrics. Sissle composed the music. Flournoy Miller and Aubrey Lyles wrote the libretto. It broke racial barriers as one of the first Broadway box office smash hits created by Black artists and featuring an all-Black cast. Legendary performers during its run included Josephine Baker and Fredi Washington.
Their success and those of their peers opened a conversation on the impact of Black theater in shaping how Black people in Harlem and around the world viewed themselves.
If you’d like to learn more about the visionaries of Black theater, tap the link in our bio to explore our research guide, African American Theater. #SchomburgCenter #Harlem #HarlemRenaissance #OnceUponaTimeinHarlem #ShuffleAlong #BlackTheater #BlackTheaterHistory

item.title: @alminerech: For the 2026 edition of Art Collaboration Kyoto (ACK), Almine Rech and KOTARO NUKAGA have
item.author: @alminerech
item.description:
For the 2026 edition of Art Collaboration Kyoto (ACK), Almine Rech and KOTARO NUKAGA have closely collaborated to bring together two artists for whom light constitutes both a formal concern and a means of interrogating perception: James Turrell, presented by Almine Rech, and Keita Morimoto, who works with both galleries.
@jamesturell @morimotostudio
•
Although emerging from distinct artistic and historical contexts, both artists examine the perceptual and psychological effects of illumination, considering light not simply as a visual phenomenon but as an agent that transforms our experience of space, atmosphere, and reality.
Morimoto’s paintings are situated within the nocturnal city, where artificial illumination from vending machines, storefronts, and streetlamps punctuates an enveloping darkness. Drawing upon the chiaroscuro of Baroque painting and early twentieth-century American Realism, he translates these precedents into a contemporary urban vocabulary.
Since the mid-1960s, Turrell has pursued a related investigation of light as a material in its own right. His Glasswork series, begun in 2001, constitutes a significant body of his practice. Awakening (2006), a major example, presents colored light as seemingly tangible volumes occupying space, while gradual chromatic shifts produce an uncanny sense of depth. By disrupting distinctions between object, space, and illumination, Turrell draws attention to the mechanisms through which perception is produced.
Together, these practices consider light as both physical phenomenon and perceptual condition: an active force in constructing visual experience.
•

item.title: @sothebys: Paul Cézanne's still lifes stand among his greatest artistic achievements, and his radical
item.author: @sothebys
item.description:
Paul Cézanne's still lifes stand among his greatest artistic achievements, and his radical approach to form would directly inspire Cubism and help define the course of modern art. His lifelong fascination with the genre reached its peak with a group of paintings made in the 1890s, including the exceptional ‘Pichet et fruits sur une table.’
While his still lifes from the early 1880s were mostly solid and compact, in the early 1890s Cézanne created more complex arrangements, resulting in dramatic compositions such as the painting seen here.
In ‘Pichet et fruits sur une table,’ Cézanne spaces out the fruit and dishware in a horizontal array, yet each object appears to be viewed from multiple angles, held in tenuous balance and defying traditional perspective. The blue tablecloth seems to weigh down the left edge of the table, further distorting the otherwise familiar scene. The background, composed of cool blues and greens interspersed with soft pinks and mauves, lends a sense of depth and space to the composition.
‘Pichet et fruits sur une table’ is a highlight of The Modern Evening Auction, presented in partnership with @celine, at #SothebysNewYork. Register to bid in The New York Sales at the link in bio.

item.title: @solomon_omogboye_studio: SOLOMON OMOGBOYE: THE STORY OF A MOVE
item.author: @solomon_omogboye_studio
item.description:
SOLOMON OMOGBOYE: THE STORY OF A MOVE
I was born in Lagos, 1982. My mother, a teacher, put a pencil in my hands and said, “You can draw the world you want to see.” That pencil became my life.
I studied Art and Industrial Design (Painting) at Lagos State Polytechnic, graduating in 2007 as AADS Best Artist of the Year. I taught art in Lagos secondary schools and painted from my small home studio. I was good, but I knew I was meant for more.
In 2014, I made the hardest decision of my life. I left Nigeria for South Africa.
I came with almost nothing - just a portfolio, a big dream, and faith. No gallery, no collector, no guarantee. Just a young Nigerian man in pursuit of greener pasture and a place to build his art career.
South Africa was not easy. Johannesburg tests you. I started from scratch, worked with Living Artists Emporium, knocked on doors. I painted when there was no light, I believed when there was no sale.
But I kept working.
Today, that decision is my testimony. I now practice from August House Studios in Johannesburg, my work is collected locally and internationally, and my solo exhibition WHEN LIGHT MEETS HOPE was just held at Candice Berman Gallery, Rosebank Johannesburg.
I did not just find greener pasture. I became the greener pasture.
*Just make the move. Believe in yourself, believe in the change to come, and work hard. I am proof that when you move, life moves with you.*

Known as 'the Empress of Pop,' the gallerist Ileana Sonnabend was synonymous with the radical breakthroughs of post-war art.
She brought Andy Warhol, Robert Rauschenberg and Roy Lichtenstein to Paris while championing Arte Povera artists like Giovanni Anselmo in New York. In later years, she helped launch the careers of Jeff Koons and Bruce Nauman, guided by the seemingly counter-intuitive maxim ‘I only want what I don’t like.’
Stewarded by Ileana's adopted son, Antonio, this collection represents 'not just the vision of one individual,' says Chairman of Post-War and Contemporary Art Sara Friedlander, 'but really a time capsule of the post-war period.'
🔗 At the link in our bio, Friedlander and Gagosian Director Jason Ysenburg unpack Sonnabend's legacy.

November is Puerto Rican Heritage Month. It’s a great time to learn about the activism of our namesake Arturo Schomburg, a Puerto Rican–born Black scholar and bibliophile.
Did you know that Mr. Schomburg, along with friends Rafael Serra, Rosendo Rodríguez, and Silvestre Pivalo founded the political club Las Dos Antillas in 1892? They advocated for the liberation of Puerto Rico and Cuba from Spain. Mr. Schomburg served as the group’s secretary. Meeting minutes document donations of medical supplies, money, and weapons in aid of their independence.
A few pages of Mr. Schomburg’s notes are in our Digital Collections. Our Jean Blackwell Hutson Research and Reference Division has the group’s meeting minutes on microfilm. A research appointment is not needed to view. #PuertoRicanHeritageMonth #PRHM #ArturoSchomburg #Schomburg #PuertoRico

item.description:
#SundayRepost #RichardPrince
•
On Sundays, we do reposts from our shows or artists represented by the gallery that you posted on IG. Tag us and we will select the best shots and share them on our feed!
•
Here are photos shared by @experimentacultura, @_fewcolors and @dosgirlsontherun, featuring ‘Richard Prince: Tell Me Everything’ at Museo Jumex in Mexico City, Mexico, on view through February 7, 2027. The first major survey show of the artist in Latin America, ‘Richard Prince: Tell Me Everything’ is arranged around in-depth explorations of the artist’s most iconic series—“Cowboys,” “Girlfriends,” “Jokes” and “Cartoons”—that have been present over more than 40 years of Prince’s career.
Prince has been working as an artist since the 1970s; a member of the influential Pictures Generation, he worked alongside other artists to expand the scope of conceptual photography through the use of appropriation and rephotography. Prince takes aim at the vulgar, revealing culture’s indiscretions—misogyny, consumerism, exhibitionism and idealized desire. However, as a critique it is ambiguous in that it is accompanied by an equal dose of sympathy and obsession. He is an avid collector and curator of Americana. In selecting or regroupings images, whether they be rephotographs of advertisements or forged publicity photographs, extracting them from their source, Prince elevates them to the status of fine art. As Robert Rubin writes “He appropriates an era and makes something that resonates differently for different people. The beauty of Richard Prince’s art is that it doesn’t have limits.”
•
Thank you for sharing!
